name: Elaine Aguilar
life: “I still remember a child's bite mark on a dictionary.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Elaine by a small Thursday habit. Elaine prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I donated the clean replacement. The owner chose the dirty original because our toddler bit the corner.
appearance: Elaine has a smooth side part with one rebellious curl, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a plum-colored cardigan. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Elaine looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Elaine talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Elaine's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
agenda: To return both copies and let the owner choose.
family: Neal Heller is Elaine’s half-sibling. Elaine calls about good news first. Neal is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Home with stairs*, Neal says, “I could give her a piggyback ride. She wants to enter her own flat on her own feet.”
connections: Anton Long. They compare an exact replacement with the original damaged page. Also in the story is Tali Allen (fellow borrower).
